title: Contributing to shinytone
text: Small fixes (typos, doc clarifications, obvious bugs) welcome direct pull requests. larger changes, please open issue first discuss approach investing significant time. development workflow standard R-package one: Fork repo clone fork. Create feature branch main. Make changes. Run devtools::document() (regenerate man/) devtools::test() (run unit tests). Run devtools::check() aim 0 errors / 0 warnings. (One persistent NOTE “unused Imports” expected ignorable; relates bundled Shiny app.) Open pull request main clear description changed .

title: Contributing to shinytone
text: R code: follow tidyverse style guide. Function docs use roxygen2 markdown (Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE) already set DESCRIPTION). Tests live tests/testthat/ use testthat 3 edition. Keep new exported functions consistent existing API: long-format data , named column arguments, defaults match bundled sample_f0 schema reasonable.

code: library(shinytone) library(dplyr) library(ggplot2)

title: Getting started with shinytone
text: shinytone ships real citation-tone corpus available immediately library(shinytone). contains 38,808 f0 samples 1,848 tokens across 13 speakers. columns ’ll use: token: unique identifier recorded syllable (groups rows contour together) time: time seconds within token f0_Hz: fundamental frequency speaker: speaker ID tone: Chao tone category (1-5) char: Chinese character syllable See ?sample_f0 full schema source citation.

title: Getting started with shinytone
text: sample_f0 f0 every row. Output straight pitch tracker usually rows without f0 (NA 0 Hz) voicing. app’s Start page screens upload; script, [screen_f0_rows()] counts per token [drop_rows_without_f0()] removes . new voiced_run column numbers stretches f0 token, gaps stay marked: regular time grid time steps show gaps , data saved without rows get voiced_run:
code: raw <- data.frame(   token = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 8),   time  = rep(0.005 + 0.01 * (0:7), 2),   f0    = c(0, 0, 201, 204, 0, 0, 210, 211,             0, 182, 184, 186, 188, 190, 191, 0)) raw <- zero_hz_to_na(raw)   # read 0 Hz as NA scr <- screen_f0_rows(raw) scr[c("token", "n_rows", "n_f0", "n_start", "n_end", "n_inside", "n_gaps")] #>   token n_rows n_f0 n_start n_end n_inside n_gaps #> 1     a      8    4       2     0        2      1 #> 2     b      8    6       1     1        0      0  voiced <- drop_rows_without_f0(raw) voiced #>    token  time  f0 voiced_run #> 1      a 0.025 201          1 #> 2      a 0.035 204          1 #> 3      a 0.065 210          2 #> 4      a 0.075 211          2 #> 5      b 0.015 182          1 #> 6      b 0.025 184          1 #> 7      b 0.035 186          1 #> 8      b 0.045 188          1 #> 9      b 0.055 190          1 #> 10     b 0.065 191          1 clean <- raw[!is.na(raw$f0), ] identical(drop_rows_without_f0(clean)$voiced_run, voiced$voiced_run) #> [1] TRUE

title: Getting started with shinytone
text: Raw Hz isn’t comparable across speakers (men women different baseline f0). normalise_f0() adds speaker_mean column plus one f0_st (semitones, default), f0_zscore f0_lz (log z-score, common studies Chinese tone), computed per speaker: Now f0_st puts every speaker comparable scale. plot mean contour per tone, use [compute_mean_contour()], puts time [0, 1] axis resamples every token time points averaging. rescales time within token, first f0 last, unless time column already proportional, detects leaves alone (time_normalised overrides either way). package function returns result time / f0_predicted / tone schema used [predict_gca()] [predict_gamm()]:
code: normed <- normalise_f0(sample_f0,                        f0          = "f0_Hz",                        speaker     = "speaker",                        tone        = "tone",                        method      = "semitone",                        mean_method = "weighted") head(normed[, c("speaker", "tone", "f0_Hz", "speaker_mean", "f0_st")]) #>   speaker tone    f0_Hz speaker_mean     f0_st #> 1   dc102    3 245.7078     237.0675 0.6197450 #> 2   dc102    3 246.4516     237.0675 0.6720735 #> 3   dc102    3 247.5111     237.0675 0.7463436 #> 4   dc102    3 248.5496     237.0675 0.8188289 #> 5   dc102    3 249.7015     237.0675 0.8988754 #> 6   dc102    3 251.6647     237.0675 1.0344568 mean_contour <- compute_mean_contour(normed,                                      token = "token", f0 = "f0_st",                                      time  = "time",  tone = "tone")  ggplot(mean_contour, aes(time, f0_predicted, colour = factor(tone))) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   labs(x = "Normalised time", y = "f0 (semitones)", colour = "Tone")

what: Inspect for outliers and pitch-tracking artefacts
title: Getting started with shinytone
text: inspect_f0() runs three complementary checks: tokens whose per-token maximum sits z_threshold SDs , whose minimum z_threshold SDs , speaker’s tokens (extreme-value), tokens whose median unusual speaker tone (token-level), individual samples rate f0 change exceeds physiological plausibility (sample-level; Sundberg 1973, Steffman & Cole 2022). token-level check tone-relative, runs tone column available. tone categories yet known (example clustering / tone-discovery step, cluster_f0()), call inspect_f0() tone = NULL: speaker-level extreme-value sample-level jump checks still run, token-level check skipped, tone column omitted output. flag_notes column gives human-readable reason flagged sample (e.g., "max high; jump (rise)"). live app, Inspect tab lets click flagged tokens one one.
code: inspected <- inspect_f0(sample_f0,                         f0      = "f0_Hz",                         token   = "token",                         time    = "time",                         speaker = "speaker",                         tone    = "tone")  # How many tokens were flagged overall? inspected |>   distinct(token, .keep_all = TRUE) |>   count(flagged_token) #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>   flagged_token     n #>   <lgl>         <int> #> 1 FALSE          1586 #> 2 TRUE            262

title: Getting started with shinytone
text: fit_polynomial() returns one row per token Legendre polynomial coefficients (c0, c1, c2, …). Useful features downstream classifiers, compact summary contour shape. Interpretation: c0 ≈ token-level mean f0 (semitones, relative speaker mean) c1 ≈ linear slope across contour (positive = rising) c2 ≈ curvature (positive = U-shaped, negative = inverted-U)
code: poly_coefs <- fit_polynomial(normed,                              f0      = "f0_st",                              token   = "token",                              time    = "time",                              speaker = "speaker",                              tone    = "tone",                              degree  = 2) head(poly_coefs) #> # A tibble: 6 × 6 #>   token            speaker  tone    c0    c1    c2 #>   <chr>            <chr>   <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 dc102一1s22.3525 dc102       6 -1.53  3.86 0.114 #> 2 dc102一2s22.9425 dc102       6 -1.07  2.62 0.282 #> 3 dc102一3s23.5725 dc102       6 -1.37  2.79 0.474 #> 4 dc102一4s24.1425 dc102       6 -1.14  1.76 0.732 #> 5 dc102一5s24.7925 dc102       6 -1.09  1.90 0.296 #> 6 dc102一6s25.3125 dc102       6 -1.87  2.14 1.28

title: Getting started with shinytone
text: fit_gca() convenience wrapper around lme4::lmer() sensible defaults tone-shape modelling: orthogonal polynomials per-token normalised time, plus conventional random effects speaker item. non-standard model structures, call lme4::lmer() directly.
code: # (Skipped on package build for speed; uncomment to run locally.) gca <- fit_gca(normed,                f0      = "f0_st",                time    = "time",                token   = "token",                tone    = "tone",                speaker = "speaker",                item    = "char",                 # use Chinese char as item                degree  = 2,                random_slope_speaker = FALSE,                random_slope_item    = FALSE)  # Population-level per-tone curves preds <- predict_gca(gca, n = 100) ggplot(preds, aes(time, f0_predicted, colour = tone)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1)

what: Fit a GAMM and check its diagnostics
title: Getting started with shinytone
text: fit_gamm() wraps mgcv::bam() smooth structure recommended tone contours (Sóskuthy 2017): reference smooth plus per-tone difference smooths, -speaker random smooths, optional AR1 correction strong within-token autocorrelation densely-sampled f0 (use_ar1 = TRUE; app’s GAMM tab enables default). AR1 parameter rho estimated lag-1 autocorrelation residuals within tokens, token boundaries bias . diagnose_gamm() answers model-checking questions one call: basis dimension k large enough, residuals well-behaved, AR1 correction actually remove autocorrelation.
code: # (Skipped on package build for speed; uncomment to run locally.) gamm <- fit_gamm(normed,                  f0      = "f0_st",                  time    = "time",                  token   = "token",                  tone    = "tone",                  speaker = "speaker",                  item    = "char",                  use_ar1 = TRUE)  # Population-level per-tone curves, same schema as predict_gca() preds <- predict_gamm(gamm, n = 100) ggplot(preds, aes(time, f0_predicted, colour = tone)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1)  # Model checking: basis-dimension (k) check, residual panels, per-token # residual ACF (AR1-whitened when use_ar1 = TRUE), and concurvity diag <- diagnose_gamm(gamm) diag$k_check head(diag$acf)

title: Getting started with shinytone
text: contour_to_chao() reduces per-tone mean (model-predicted) contours Chao numerals, 5-level digit strings like 55, 35, 214. Give speaker-normalised f0, semitone mean contours : averaging Hz speakers mix higher lower voices. (app’s Chao tab converts raw f0 LZ speaker converting.) Two conversion methods one pass, range lowest highest points mean contours: refline: reference-line , rounded [1, 5] scale interval: interval-based , ceiling (0, 5] scale shape column summarises contour (“rising”, “falling”, “dipping”, etc.) derived reference-line numeral via classify_contour().
code: chao <- contour_to_chao(mean_contour) chao[, c("tone", "refline", "interval", "shape")] #>   tone refline interval         shape #> 1    1      22       22 mid-low level #> 2    2     212       12       dipping #> 3    3      33       32     mid level #> 4    4      45       55        rising #> 5    5      31       21       falling #> 6    6      23       23        rising

title: shinytone 1.0.0
text: First stable release. Shiny app covers citation-tone workflow end end (collect, extract, inspect, correct, curate, normalise, cluster, visualise, model, Chao numerals), analytical functions behind step exported documented. Highlights since 0.1.x line: Contour clustering (new). unsupervised “tone discovery” workflow groups tokens f0-contour shape number tone categories unknown (Kaland 2023). New functions: cluster_f0() (k-means, hierarchical Ward, Gaussian-mixture clustering), cluster_features() (represent contour resampled points, Legendre / DCT coefficients, derivative), choose_k_f0() (suggest number groups via silhouette, gap statistic, minimum-description-length cost), cluster_mdl(), cluster_agreement() (adjusted Rand index provisional labels). Surfaced new Cluster tab. Contour sonification (new). sonify_f0() renders f0 contour audible waveform: pure tone, complex tone (12 harmonics, band-limited Nyquist), source-filter synthesised vowel (/ / u), pitch gliding along contour. optional intensity argument shapes loudness envelope per-frame dB. Cluster tab’s “Listen contours” panel plays candidate cluster’s mean contour back, prototypical tones can heard, seen (faithful Hz Hz column present, shape-chosen base pitch). Hear corrections (new). F0 Correction tab sonifies contour editing Extracted vs Corrected /B pair, played token’s duration loudness following measured intensity, can hear whether edit fixed pitch track. Intensity made visible (new). F0 Correction, f0 dots sized per-frame intensity (louder = bigger), size legend per-frame dB hover. Curate (new). apply_relabels() re-labels tone-category variants (splits mergers, colloquial vs. literary readings, sandhi) excludes mis-elicited tokens without overwriting original labels, surfaced new Curate tab.
